test_title: PYST 12 - SSC CHSL 2025 - English Language (Held On: 17 Nov, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: english
question:
**Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect voice.**

"Who is singing so beautifully?" the judge asked.

options.text: The judge asked who was singing so beautifully.
The judge asked who is singing so beautifully.
The judge asked who had been singing so beautifully.
The judge asked who singing so beautifully was.

solution:
The correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Direct Speech:** "Who is singing so beautifully?" the judge asked.
 
• **Key Conversions:**
 
 
• **Sentence Structure (Interrogative to Assertive):**
 
 
• When converting a question into indirect speech, the sentence structure changes from interrogative (verb before subject) to assertive (subject before verb).
 
• The question format **"is singing"** becomes the statement format **"was singing."**
 
 
 
• **Tense Change (Backshifting):**
 
 
• Since the reporting verb **"asked"** is in the past tense, the present continuous **"is singing"** shifts back to the past continuous **"was singing."**
 
 
 
• **Punctuation and Connectors:**
 
 
• The question mark is removed.
 
• For 'Wh-' questions (who, what, where, etc.), the 'Wh-' word itself acts as the connector, so no additional conjunction like "that" or "if" is needed.
 
 
 
 

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"The judge asked who was singing so beautifully."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2:** Fails to shift the tense from "is" to "was."
 
• **Option 3:** Uses the past perfect continuous ("had been singing"), which would only be correct if the original sentence was in the past continuous ("Who was singing?") or present perfect continuous ("Who has been singing?").
 
• **Option 4:** Uses an incorrect and awkward word order that does not follow standard English syntax for reported speech.
